q: 1. The art of representation of an object by systemic lines on a paper is known as
explain: Drawing is the technical method of representing an object's shape and features using lines on a flat surface.

q: 2. Drawing is the ................of engineers.
explain: Engineering drawing is considered the universal language of engineers because it conveys technical information across different regions and languages without ambiguity.

q: 3. Vertical lines are drawn
explain: Standard drafting practice is to draw vertical lines from top to bottom for better control and visibility of the line being drawn.

q: 4. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has
explain: Good freehand sketching needs skill (proficiency), repeated practice, and patience together, not any single quality alone.

q: 5. Pencil of ......grade sharpened in the form of ........ is used for sketching.
explain: Sketching requires a softer lead (like HB or B) and a conical point to allow for free-hand movement and varied line weight.

q: 6. Free hand sketches are used for expressing and recording .............
explain: Freehand sketches are a quick way to record and communicate a concept or new idea before it is developed into a formal, scaled drawing.

q: 7. In sketching, horizontal lines are draw from .............
explain: For right-handed drafters, the natural and recommended direction for sketching horizontal lines freehand is left to right, for better control and visibility of the line being drawn.

q: 8. The space between two sentences should be left equal to
explain: For legibility in technical lettering, spacing between sentences is typically twice the height of the letters used.

q: 9. The main objective of writing letters/alphabets on the drawing is to make the drawing
explain: Lettering provides vital non-graphical information such as titles, materials, notes, and specific measurements.

q: 10. Horizontal lines are drawn
explain: Horizontal lines can technically be drawn either way, though standard practice for right-handed drafters is left-to-right.

q: 11. Vertical lines are drawn
explain: Vertical lines are drawn using a set square, moving either from top-to-bottom or bottom-to-top.

q: 12. The technique for freehand sketch to drawing straight line is .............
explain: When sketching a straight line freehand, the recommended technique is to first fix/mark the required length of the line before drawing it lightly between the points.

q: 13. In sketching, horizontal lines are drawn from
explain: For a right-handed person, drawing horizontal lines left to right gives better control and visibility.

q: 14. Size of letter means the …… of the letter.
explain: Letter 'size' in drafting standards refers to the height of the capital letters.

q: 15. Sketching is usually done
explain: Sketching, by definition, is done freehand without the aid of drafting instruments.

q: 16. What is the slant for the letter shown?
explain: Italic or slanted lettering in engineering drawing usually deviates by approximately 10 to 15 degrees from the vertical.

q: 17. What is the aspect ratio for the letter shown?
explain: Aspect ratio is the ratio of width to height. If a letter is half as wide as it is tall, the ratio is 0.5.

q: 18. Free hand drawing is done for
explain: It is a versatile tool used both for early ideation and for making quick on-site corrections to existing plans.

q: 19. In engineering field free hand drawing is mostly used for
explain: It allows an engineer to quickly communicate complex visual ideas to a client or team member without needing instruments.

q: 20. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing circle is
options: fixing a fixed point and arc
explain: One technique involves fixing the center point with a finger and rotating the paper, or marking points at an equal radius.

q: 21. Which of the following is not intended while making a sketch in the context of technical drawings?
options: A quick way to record an idea for work
A way to try out different ideas
explain: A technical sketch is meant to be a quick, preliminary tool for recording and exploring ideas — it is explicitly not intended to be a finished, final product.

q: 22. Which of the following is not intended while making a 'sketch' in the context of technical drawings?
options: a quick way to record and idea an idea for work
explain: A sketch is meant as a quick, preliminary freehand record of an idea, not a finished (final) product.

q: 23. Vertical lines are drawn .............
explain: The standard drafting convention for drawing vertical lines (especially freehand or with a T-square/set-square) is to draw from top to bottom for better control and visibility.

q: 24. Free hand sketching can be done only when, one has
explain: Technical sketching requires a combination of hand-eye skill (proficiency), repetition (practice), and care (patience).

q: 25. Sketching is usually done:
explain: By definition, a sketch is a quick, freehand drawing.

q: 26. Which of the following is not intended while making a ‘sketch’ in the context of technical drawings ?
options: a quick way to record an idea for work
explain: A sketch is by definition preliminary and quick; it is not meant to be the final 'finished' or 'polished' product.

q: 27. Engineers prefer to make ......... sketches than to pictorial sketches to clear the shape of an object.
explain: Orthographic sketches provide exact dimensions and multiple views (top, front, side), making them more practical for engineering than pictorial views.

q: 28. The free hand drawing of an ordinary room is generally :
explain: Internal views of rooms are most commonly sketched using two-point perspective to show two walls receding to different vanishing points.

q: 29. The most suitable tool to draw freehand is:
explain: An HB pencil, being of medium hardness, gives good control and line quality for freehand sketching.

q: 30. The drawing prepared by a pencil without use of drawing instrument is called .............
explain: A drawing made using only a pencil, without T-squares, set squares, compasses, or other instruments, is called a freehand sketch.

q: 31. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has .............
explain: Good freehand sketching requires a combination of skill/proficiency, regular practice, and patience together, making 'all of these' the correct comprehensive answer.

q: 32. The type of pencil used to lettering guide lines is
explain: A hard 2H pencil is used to draw faint, thin guide lines for lettering that won't smudge or dominate the final lettering.

q: 33. The tool used for proportioning of objects to the paper while preparing a free hand drawing is generally:
explain: In freehand sketching, the pencil itself (held at arm's length) is commonly used to visually judge and proportion the object onto the paper.

q: 34. Freehand sketching can be done only when one has
explain: Good freehand sketching requires skill, practice and patience together.

q: 35. Free hand sketch is normally used for .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'final' is marked correct; conventionally freehand sketches are used for quick concept development and discussion rather than as final deliverables, but the given key selects option (b).

q: 36. The most suitable tool to draw freehand is .............
explain: An HB pencil, with its medium hardness/softness, provides good control and visibility for general freehand sketching, making it the most suitable common tool among the options.

q: 37. Free hand sketching can be done only when one has .............
explain: As with the earlier repeated item, effective freehand sketching requires a combination of patience and good practice together, supporting the 'all of the above' answer.

q: 38. Concept drawing is normally provided for the work of .............
explain: A concept drawing represents the initial design idea and is prepared before construction begins, to communicate and finalize the overall design intent.

q: 39. The techniques for free hand sketch to drawing straight line is .............
explain: Effective freehand straight-line sketching typically combines fixing the two end points, judging the overall length, and marking the midpoint as guides, so 'all of the above' applies.
